name: AT&T 8525
pros: Wi-Fi support (Wi-Fi 802.11b/g) for data-free browsing and connectivity
2 MP camera capable of capturing good photos for its release era
Li-Po 1350 mAh battery offers solid operating endurance for daily use
cons: No official IP rating for dust or water resistance
Standard charging speeds without ultra-fast charging support

reviews.title: Solid performance for its 2006 launch era
reviews.body: Picking this up around its release period, the Microsoft Windows Mobile 6 Professional experience felt snappy and responsive for the price tier. The 2 MP camera delivered reliable shots in outdoor lighting.

reviews.title: Reliable battery and daily usability
reviews.body: The Li-Po 1350 mAh power cell paired with AT&T's software tuning easily lasted through a full work day with mixed web browsing, calls, and media playback.

reviews.title: Refined hardware styling and build
reviews.body: The physical chassis of the AT&T 8525 feels well-balanced in hand. Its 113 x 58 x 22 mm (4.45 x 2.28 x 0.87 in) make it easy to hold during long daily sessions.

reviews.title: Great value for the hardware specifications
reviews.body: For the price point, getting standard platform performance alongside 64MB RAM storage, microSDHC slot made the AT&T 8525 an easy recommendation among rivals in 2006.

reviews.title: Smooth day-to-day software responsiveness
reviews.body: Operating on Microsoft Windows Mobile 6 Professional, the user interface is intuitive with smooth system transitions. Core apps and browsing run without noticeable stutter.

reviews.title: Dependable display and audio clarity
reviews.body: The screen (Removable Li-Po 1350 mAh battery, 2.8", 240x320 pixels) produces vibrant colors for video streaming, and call clarity through the earpiece is crystal clear.

reviews.title: A well-rounded package from AT&T
reviews.body: Overall, the AT&T 8525 proved to be a durable and well-engineered mobile device representing AT&T's design philosophy nicely.
